source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν πλὴν τῶν κανονικῶν ψαλτῶν, τῶν ἐπὶ τὸν ἄμβωνα ἀναβαινόντων, καὶ ἀπὸ διφθέρας ψαλλόντων, ἑτέρους τινὰς ψάλλειν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Ἐμποδίζει ὁ παρών Κανών τὸ νά ψάλλη εἰς τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν ὁποῖος θέλει, ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ Ψάλται οἱ κανονικοί, οἱ ἐν τῷ Κλήρῳ δηλ. συνηριθμημένοι καὶ χειροτονημένοι εἰς κάθε Ἐκκλησίαν, οἵτινες ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐπ’ ἄμβωνος, καὶ ψάλλουσιν μὲ ψαλτικὰς μεμβράνας(διφθέραι γὰρ τὰ δέρματα ὀνομάζονται, ἐξ ὢν γίνονται αἱ μεμβρᾶναι) (1) ἢ καὶ χαρτίνας. Ἀταξία γὰρ ἀκολουθεῖ καὶ χασμωδία ἐὰν ψάλλη ὁποῖος τύχει ἀμαθής, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου εὐταξία, ὅταν ψάλλουν οἱ διωρισμένοι Ψάλται, καὶ ψαλτικῶν ἔμπειροι. Ὅρᾳ καὶ τὸν οε΄. τῆς ς΄.
thought_title: Only canonical singers may chant in church
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its canons; this canon regulates who may chant in church, and the source includes the canon heading, the canon text, and a later Greek interpretation.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning that it is not necessary, except the canonical singers, those going up onto the ambo and chanting from parchment, for any others to chant in church. Interpretation. The present Canon hinders that whoever wants should chant in the Church, but only the canonical Singers, that is, those numbered in the Clergy and ordained for each Church, who go up onto an ambo and chant with musical membranes (for skins are called diphtherai, from which membranes are made) or also paper ones. For disorder follows and discordant noise if whoever happens to be unlearned chants, and on the contrary good order, when the appointed Singers chant, and those experienced in chanting. See also canon 75 of the 6th.

lemmas.gloss: ordained, appointed by laying on of hands

choices.why: The glossary cast lists Singers as canonical cantors; 'canonical' preserves the technical sense of enrolled and ordained.
The interpretation explains diphtherai as skins from which membranes are made; 'parchment' captures the material sense.
The verb means to block or prevent; 'hinders' keeps the force of the canon's prohibition.
The word denotes bad singing or cacophony; 'discordant noise' conveys the disorderly sound.
The term refers to appointment by laying on of hands, standard for clergy; 'ordained' is the natural English equivalent.

pass_b_english: Concerning the rule that no one except the canonical singers, who go up onto the ambo and chant from parchment, may sing in church. Interpretation. The present canon hinders just anyone from singing in the church; only the canonical singers may do so—that is, those who are enrolled in the clergy and ordained in each church. These go up onto the ambo and chant from parchment sheets (for diphtherai is the name for the skins from which parchment sheets are made), or from paper ones. For disorder and discordant noise follow if some untrained person happens to sing, and on the contrary good order follows when the appointed singers, experienced in chanting, do the singing. See also canon 75 of the Sixth Council.
notes: The source text is a canon heading followed by a later Greek interpretation (Ἐρμηνεία), not the original canon text itself; the interpretation is included in the source and translated as such.
